server.name: Netzo API
server.title: Netzo
server.description: Netzo is an operational ERP. Agents read and update a company's live records across sales and customers, purchasing and suppliers, inventory and warehouses, logistics, manufacturing, point of sale, services, HR and finance, and build reports, charts and documents from them. Access follows the signed-in user's module roles (OAuth) or an organization API key.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Never invent field names or fabricate row data. Start with list_tables, then describe_table before reading or writing an unfamiliar table. If list_tables fails, quote its message and stop: the connection grants no tables (an authorization issue, not a connection failure). Read with find / count / get / aggregate. Pagination is { page, pageSize } (max 50), not limit/skip. Write only after describe_table. Prefer archive over delete. Destructive tools need confirm:true or elicitation. Quote locale labels (from list_tables, describe_table, fieldLabels) in backticks for the user; tool names, tableUid and row keys stay UIDs. For host UI use the Netzo Apps: find-table (columns), page-list / page-grid / page-gallery (cards), record-card (one row), kpi-stat (one number), chart (Netzo fetches and aggregates the data; never pass numbers). Files and PDFs: get_skill { name: "netzo-mcp-read", ref: "files" }. Netzo renders charts, PDFs and reports itself; do not look for another MCP for them.

SKILLS: before multi-step work (import, analyse, reconcile, triage, reports…), call list_skills, then get_skill with the matching name and follow it. Platform skills: netzo-mcp-discover, netzo-mcp-read, netzo-mcp-write, netzo-mcp-import, netzo-mcp-attach, netzo-reports-author.

tool.name: action
tool.title: Run Procedure
tool.description: Run any procedure without a dedicated tool: lifecycle and special actions (archive, approve, process, createInvoice, …), duplicate, and the read shape findReferences. Non-table procedures use the namespace as tableUid (pricing.resolve, compositions.ensure). Call `describe_table` first: its `actions` list each procedure with its policy and `data` fields. Record procedures take `id` (+ optional `data`); query procedures take only `data` as their input. Most procedures write: they change record state, may create related records (e.g. createInvoice), and some reach external services (e.g. fiscal stamping with the PAC); a state change such as approve may not be undoable. Consequential actions require confirm:true or elicitation. Returns the procedure result plus, for record procedures, `id`, `message`, `link`, and `next` (follow-up procedures this connection may run).

tool.name: attach_file
tool.title: Attach File
tool.description: Use a file staged by upload_file. mode "preview": run the blob field's document extractor and return the fields the file would establish (writes nothing). mode "slot": store the file in the record's blob field `uid` (e.g. a CFDI `xml`), replacing the file already there. mode "file": add the file to the record's files list as source evidence. tool.name: describe_table
tool.title: Describe Table
tool.description: Describe one table (or namespace) before reading or writing it. Always call this before creating or updating records. For a table, returns: `tableUid`, `label`, `description`, `moduleUid`, `moduleLabel`; `fields` (field UID, locale label, semantic type) and `semanticTypes`; `row` / `rowWithRelations` (JSON Schema of a row) and `createInput` / `updateInput` (JSON Schema, null when the table has none); `relations` (relation key for `with` on find/get → cardinality and related table); `allowedProcedures` / `procedures` (what this connection may call); `actions` (per-procedure description, policy and `action.data` input fields); `events` (what the table announces, which webhooks and notification templates subscribe to); and `information` (semantic table facts). For a namespace from list_tables (e.g. "pricing"), returns `namespace` and `procedures` (each with its summary and input JSON Schema).

Call describe_table first for field UIDs and semanticTypes. Returns the plotted data as text.
